title: Augmenting Simulated Noisy Quantum Data Collection by Orders of Magnitude Using Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
problem: Classical simulation of noisy quantum systems requires 2^n x 2^n-dimensional density matrices for n qubits, making even moderate system sizes computationally intractable. Quantum trajectory methods reduce overhead but use unoptimized sampling, redundant state preparation, and single-shot data collection.
motivation: Large-scale noisy quantum simulation is critical for validating quantum error correction and understanding realistic quantum hardware behavior. Current implementations waste compute cycles through redundant operations and suboptimal data collection strategies.
method: Pre-Trajectory Sampling technique optimizes trajectory simulation by: (1) tailoring error types to match experimental conditions, (2) batching sampling without redundant computation, (3) collecting error information efficiently. Evaluation on statevector simulation of 35-qubit quantum error-correction code and tensor network simulation of 85 qubits.
key_novelty: Optimized sampling strategy for trajectory-based quantum simulation combining error type tailoring, batch processing, and efficient error information collection.
contributions: Pre-Trajectory Sampling technique reducing simulation overhead
Statevector simulation of 35-qubit QEC code with up to 106x speedup
Tensor network simulation of 85 qubits with 16x speedup
Massive dataset generation: 1 trillion shots (35-qubit) and 1 million shots (85-qubit)
Optimization strategies for batch sampling without redundant computation
Error-aware data collection for realistic quantum noise modeling
baselines: standard trajectory method with unoptimized sampling
limitations: Limited to simulating up to 85 qubits; tensor network approach scalability beyond this size not explored.
primary_theme: Quantum circuit simulation and error correction
